description: sign_bytes_ed25519 writes plaintext-to-sign and raw signature files into the SAME DIRECTORY as the private key (skills/_shared/lib/ed25519_util.py:124-125): `data_path = priv_path.parent / f'.signdata-{id(data):x}.tmp'` and `sig_path = priv_path.parent / f'.sigout-{id(data):x}.tmp'`. Three real problems: (1) In production, if the anicca-bot key is stored under a strict-permission directory like ~/.openclaw/identity/ (Sprint-4 documented location, spec §6), that directory may be 0o500 or otherwise not writable by the signing process — sign will fail with 'openssl sign failed rc=1' with no clear reason (REQ-C2 says raise SigningError, but the caller cannot distinguish 'writable dir' from 'key corrupt'). (2) `id(data)` for identical immutable bytes objects (e.g. b'') can collide across concurrent callers because CPython interns small immutables — two concurrent sign() invocations racing on the same data value overwrite each other's tmp files (EDGE-E10 concurrency claim in spec §4 is not satisfied for the same-payload case). (3) The verify path correctly uses `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` (line 166) for isolation — sign should use the same pattern for consistency and safety. Recommendation: use `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` inside sign_bytes_ed25519 (identical to the verify pattern) to keep private-key directories untouched and eliminate the id(data) collision.

evidence.snippet:
priv_path = Path(privkey_pem)
if not priv_path.is_file():
    raise SigningError("private key not found (path scrubbed)")
# Write data to temp file (openssl -rawin reads from -in file)
data_path = priv_path.parent / f".signdata-{id(data):x}.tmp"
sig_path = priv_path.parent / f".sigout-{id(data):x}.tmp"
